gitobj.description: one Git object; its entity id is its SHA-1 object id, so writing the same object twice writes one row

type.description: the object type, as written in the object's own header

size.description: the body's length in bytes, as written in that same header

blob.description: where an object's bytes are: their address in the @yaks/blob store

sha.description: the SHA-256 of the bytes; for a Git blob this is the file's own address in the store, not a re-encoded copy

tree_entry.description: a tree holds a child under a name; packing follows these edges to find every reachable object

name.description: the child's name in this tree; one object can be a child of several trees under different names, so the name belongs to the link

mode.description: the mode as the tree body writes it: 100644 for a file, 40000 for a directory

parent.description: this commit's parent; the edge's `ord` property keeps the parent order

compat.description: Git's compat object id: the same object's SHA-256 id, keyed by its SHA-1 id, so a client may ask for either (Git's hash-function transition, stored as key rows)

ref.description: where one branch of one repository points; one row per repository and branch name, so moving a branch updates the row that is already there

app.description: the entity the repository belongs to; deleting it deletes its branches

name.description: the branch's full name: refs/heads/main, not main

commit.description: the commit object the branch points at

target.description: for a symbolic ref, the full name it points at; absent for a direct ref

oid.description: the raw Git object id the ref names; an annotated tag need not point directly at a commit

present.description: false once a ref that was observed on this machine has been deleted

repository.description: A local Git object database, identified by its canonical common Git directory.

common.description: canonical absolute common Git directory; the entity id is derived from it

origin.description: where it is published: the remote it was cloned from or pushes to

worktree.description: A local checkout. Its identity is the repository plus the canonical checkout root, not the branch or HEAD.

gitdir.description: this worktree's own Git administrative directory

head.description: the object id HEAD resolves to; absent when the branch has no commits yet

branch.description: the shared ref entity HEAD is attached to; absent for a detached HEAD

managed.description: created by this package; it never implies automatic cleanup

checkout.description: A stored request to create a checkout on this machine; ready only once Git has succeeded. A failed request keeps its error so it can be retried.

requested.description: the base as the caller wrote it, while base holds the commit id it resolved to

target.description: the work this commit is about

message.description: the whole commit message, not just its first line

commit.description: a commit that landed, attached to the work it is about; the commit sha is the entity id, so recording the same commit twice gives one entity

path.description: the path from the repository root, as Git spells it

repository.description: the repository entity the path is read in

file.description: a file in a repository, as an entity, so anything in the graph can refer to one; its entity id is derived from the path and the repository

commit.description: the commit entity, whose id is the commit sha

revision.description: the commit a citation was last checked against; the verify step moves it to the commit checked out then

lines.description: the line range a citation names, when no definition fits

text.description: the quoted text, stored by content address

quote.description: what the citing side quoted, so a reader sees what it saw without opening the file

cites_check.title: Check citations
cites_check.description: Report citations that moved or were never checked. A `cites` edge can point to a file or symbol in this checkout, or any other graph entity. For a file, Git answers which commits after `revision.commit` touched the named place. For another entity, its current content hash is compared with `cites.hash`, recorded when verified; this needs no journal or checkout. A citation nobody checked is unverified, and one without enough evidence is unknown. Scope with `of` (only citations one entity makes) or `path` (only citations of one file). Returns a report in content.body with warning or failure findings. It writes nothing and enforces nothing.

of.description: only the citations this record makes; pass its id or registered name

path.description: only citations of this file path, as Git spells it

cites_verify.title: Verify a citation
cites_verify.description: Record that a citation was checked and holds. For a file or symbol, write the `verified` mark and move its `revision` to this checkout's commit. For another entity, write the mark and its current content hash in `cites.hash`, without needing a checkout. Takes the citation edge itself, or an entity, meaning every citation it makes. Returns the citations as written.

cite.description: the citation to mark; pass its id

of.description: a record, meaning every citation it makes

land.title: Land the current branch
land.description: Land the branch the current checkout is on. Fast-forwards it into the base branch (the one the shared checkout has checked out) and pushes if the base has an upstream. If the base has moved, rebases the branch onto it and returns without merging, printing what the rebase pulled in so the caller can re-run its tests and land again; that counts as a failure, because nothing landed. Refuses to land when a file would end up with content no commit on the branch wrote, unless allow-revert names that file. Runs no tests and reads no graph: everything comes from Git, in the checkout assigned to this tool call by the host (the CLI uses its current directory). Returns Git’s output and the landed commit SHA in content.body. No arguments are needed for an ordinary landing.

allow-revert.description: comma-separated paths whose reverted content is intended; they land with a warning
